# 🎯 Top 5 to comment on

### 1. [Social media users end up on government list for speaking out against Prevent](https://news.google.?oc=5)
*Freedom of speech · Metro.co.uk*

Social media users have reportedly been placed on a government-linked list after criticising Prevent, the counter-terrorism programme. The story raises serious questions about whether peaceful political or religious speech is being monitored as extremism.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** Bernard Randall was dismissed and reported to Prevent after a school sermon telling pupils they did not have to accept LGBT ideology; this is the same pattern of counter-terror language being turned on lawful dissent.

**Who this hits:** This affects parents, teachers, chaplains and ordinary Christians who post or speak about schools, ideology or government policy. It means a comment made in good faith could be treated as something suspicious rather than as lawful disagreement.

**Angle:** Our line is that Prevent must target genuine radicalisation, not become a dragnet for unpopular opinions. Viewers will understand why vague extremism categories matter in real life, and why they should ask schools, councils and employers what counts as a Prevent concern before attending training or reporting others.

**Opening line:** "Could criticising a government programme put your name on a list?"

**Title:** *Why Are Prevent Critics Ending Up on Government Lists?*

### 2. [Tribunal begins into nurse’s discrimination claim against RCN](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiwAFBVV95cUxQcFQtOUtYTUR4c0dlSzZxNlg3RVR0LUpNclh5WnBLQzI3NXFBWU1JUXQxSlpTeEdkZlJId2xCTThPR3JXMnA3OVN1TFdvYmFmR2d4LTY4QXZRUTZrRmpWSGRDOThaWmZQYVlDWHNCdDlyWHZpdmIyeERUMC05SmI0bXpiVU9MUWFnZ3Q1NEZxRVM0dW5VOHQ0MXM1RnBMWkZ3NWNGbjRCY2hseExEb2hSSzNKT3hCaXdfUFJvaVJQazQ?oc=5)
*Gender · Nursing Times*

A tribunal has begun hearing a nurse’s discrimination claim against the Royal College of Nursing. The case comes amid growing conflict over sex, gender identity and whether nurses can raise safeguarding or single-sex concerns without being punished.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** The Darlington Nurses were told to 'broaden their mindset' after objecting to sharing a changing room with a biological male identifying as a woman; Jennifer Melle also faces disciplinary action after a pronoun-related incident in an NHS setting.

**Who this hits:** This affects nurses, midwives and healthcare assistants who are being asked to accept new workplace rules on sex and gender. It also affects female patients who assume hospitals and professional bodies will protect privacy, dignity and single-sex care.

**Angle:** Our line is that nurses should not have to choose between their conscience, the law on sex, and their careers. Viewers will understand that these disputes are not abstract culture-war rows: they decide what staff may say, what women may object to, and whether professional bodies will defend or discipline them.

**Opening line:** "What happens when a nurse says biological sex still matters?"

**Title:** *Nurse Takes RCN to Tribunal Over Sex and Gender Discrimination Claim*

### 3. [Grandma, 83, 'euthanised against her will' died ‘covered in blood' after failed first attempt as probe launched](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMimAFBVV95cUxQX1dkY21CZGRvTHpRTjhHWXBzZWJaMjhLOHAtajMzOXM5SUZSMDdMQkxPeTMzYzBPMnF2WGl2X1pxa3JmWk5Tc3gxNHFOWUhYZFV1aXYyZ2g0d205bnY4Q1dBQWFib21KQUQtLWFEMEQwdl9zYjlGdkxRLTdaZGZuR1FSVnUzbDkxVzZHSlVRZE5yVUppTGV4MQ?oc=5)
*End of life · The Sun*

An 83-year-old grandmother was reportedly euthanised against her will, with claims that a first attempt failed and that she died in horrific circumstances. A probe has now been launched into what happened.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** Rashid Abbasi, Sudiksha Thirumalesh and Indi Gregory all involved families fighting life-ending medical decisions made against their wishes; while this story concerns euthanasia, it exposes the same danger when vulnerable patients lose control at the end of life.

**Who this hits:** This affects anyone with an elderly parent or grandparent who may one day depend on doctors, care homes or officials to act in their best interests. It also affects MPs and voters being told that assisted dying laws can be made completely safe.

**Angle:** Our line is that the question is not whether safeguards sound compassionate on paper, but what happens when real people are frail, frightened or unable to fight the system. Viewers will see why Christians warn against a culture where death becomes a treatment option, and why they should press MPs on enforcement, coercion and palliative care before any vote.

**Opening line:** "If safeguards fail once, who pays the price?"

**Title:** *Euthanasia Horror Story Shows Why Assisted Dying Safeguards Are Not Enough*

### 4. [UK Police Impartiality Undermined by Muslim Staff Networks Who Defend Terror Groups: Report](https://news.google.?oc=5)
*Islam · breitbart.com*

A report claims that Muslim staff networks within UK policing have undermined impartiality by defending or excusing extremist groups. If accurate, it raises urgent questions about neutrality, public confidence and the treatment of those who question Islamism.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** Luke Salmons, a police community support officer, was suspended and forced to resign after questioning Islam during mandatory diversity training; this story highlights the double standard when criticism is punished but Islamist apologetics may be tolerated inside institutions.

**Who this hits:** This affects police officers who feel unable to speak honestly in diversity training, and members of the public who need confidence that police will deal with Islamism impartially. It also matters for Christians and others who have been warned, disciplined or investigated for asking legitimate questions about Islam.

**Angle:** Our line is that the police must be politically and religiously impartial: neither anti-Muslim prejudice nor Islamist influence should be protected. Viewers will understand why internal staff networks are not harmless if they shape training, complaints or discipline, and why whistleblowers need protection.

**Opening line:** "Can the police tackle extremism if they cannot even name it?"

**Title:** *Report Raises Alarm Over Islamist Influence Inside UK Policing*

### 5. [Trans group seeks to intervene over Hampstead Heath ponds](https://news.google.?oc=5)
*Gender · leighday.co.uk*

A trans group is seeking to intervene in a dispute involving Hampstead Heath’s bathing ponds, where the question of single-sex spaces has become legally and politically contested. The case comes after the Supreme Court clarified the meaning of sex in equality law.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** The Darlington Nurses’ case is directly relevant: they objected to sharing a changing room with a biological male identifying as a woman, showing how single-sex protections affect ordinary women in everyday spaces.

**Who this hits:** This affects women and girls using changing rooms, swimming ponds, gyms and leisure facilities who expect single-sex spaces to mean biological sex. It also affects councils and service providers deciding whether to follow the law clearly or reinterpret it under pressure.

**Angle:** Our line is that single-sex spaces exist for privacy, dignity and safety, and public bodies must not pretend the law is unclear. Viewers will know to ask their council, gym, school or hospital a simple question: are your women-only spaces based on biological sex, in line with the Supreme Court judgment?

**Opening line:** "When a sign says women-only, what does it actually mean?"

**Title:** *Hampstead Heath Ponds Case Tests Single-Sex Spaces After Supreme Court Ruling*
